For information only — not financial advice. Option taxation is complex; confirm with a tax professional.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter the number of vested shares you can exercise.
  2. Enter the strike (exercise) price and the current fair market value per share.
  3. Choose ISO or NSO for the tax note.
  4. Read the cost to exercise, the spread value, and the break-even price.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the spread?

Fair market value minus strike price, times shares. It is the paper gain you capture by exercising.

What does underwater mean?

The FMV is below the strike price, so exercising now would lose money. The spread shows as negative.

How are ISOs and NSOs taxed differently?

Broadly: NSOs are taxed as ordinary income on the spread at exercise; ISOs can qualify for capital-gains treatment if holding rules are met but may trigger AMT. See a tax professional.
